intent.content:
# Intent - phase-bj: mechanical close flow

Written 2026-10-18 by fenix from Rand's rulings of 2026-10-18 (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, docs PR atm-bd-orchestration #342). One page at most. Jev questions are judged against the anchors, not this document.

## What this plan is for

Dev work is not complete until sanity verifies it, and nothing between a dev
push and the QA assignment should need the lead. Today the dev closes its own
task on push, the lead hand-assigns every sanity and QA task, and atm-bd has
never issued an assignment because its dispatch reads branch and worktree
from beads the pour never wrote them to. This phase makes the dev, fix,
sanity and qa closes one script, `atm-task-close.py`, that verifies the
minimum (PR open on `pr_target`, pushed head, rebased), closes the bead,
reports to the lead and assigns the next bead as the phase lead; the dev's
task stays open until sanity passes.

## What success looks like

- A dev or fix bead closes only through the hook; the dev's ATM task is closed by the sanity hook on PASS and the dev waits meanwhile.
- Sanity and QA assignment never need the lead: the hook assigns, atm-bd assigns a ready bead with no task, both as the phase lead.
- A sanity FAIL reopens the bead and sends the dev `sanity-rejected` on the same task and branch; `max_sanity_rounds` (default 5) escalates to the lead.
- The pour writes branch, worktree, pr_target and difficulty to every bead of a sprint family and a pydantic model per bead kind validates the whole phase.
- atm-core issue #1873 (task transition hooks, 1.6.2) is the long-term home; the skill script stands in until it ships.
- Sanity links the layer on PASS under the stack bead's claim: the stack bead holds the whole stack as ledger and lock, first PASS wins the top and the loser gets `rebase-required` (no round counted); a sanity-stack subagent handles one next-top layer per spawn, sequentially, with a lean mode and a lock timeout that never blocks the team.

## What is deliberately out of scope

- Mechanical dev or fix assignment: the lead picks the dev (ANC-060).
- Whole-stack verification in the hook: the lead owns stack hygiene (ANC-054, ANC-062).
- The small phase-bi console fixes (self-addressed send, icons, agent rows): they close in phase-bi.

## Anchors

The phase-bi anchors (ANC-001..050, REQ-BI6-AC6) are carried unchanged in
`anchors.json` so Jev judges phase-bj items against the same console
rulings; ANC-051..086 are this phase's; ANC-063 and ANC-074 are retired and replaced by ANC-078..083 and ANC-084..086, respectively (ANC-062 retired to ANC-065). Rendered to `anchors.md`.

criteria.no: The item does not plan this: it is silent, only mentions limiting rounds in general, or leaves out or changes the count, the repository setting, the default of five, or escalation on the FAIL that reaches the limit.
criteria.unclear: The item plans part of the cap and it cannot be determined whether the rest is planned.
criteria.yes: The item plans the per-bead round count, the repository-configurable limit with five as the default, and escalation to the lead instead of reopening on the FAIL that reaches the limit, as rules or as a worked sequence.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` plan the sanity round cap in `anchor.statement`: sanity FAIL rounds are counted per sanity bead (for example in `sanity_round`), the number of rounds allowed comes from the repository's `max_sanity_rounds` setting with five used when it is not set, and the FAIL that reaches the allowed number goes to the lead instead of reopening the checked bead? The plan may state these as rules or as a worked sequence of rounds, for example the fifth FAIL escalating when nothing is configured and a configured value of 2 escalating on the second FAIL. Judge presence of this plan only, not conflict.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item is irreconcilable with the rule: it follows the rule, says nothing about the round limit, or plans only behaviour the rule allows.
criteria.unclear: The item might or might not conflict with the rule; its wording does not settle it.
criteria.yes: The item plans behaviour that cannot be reconciled with the anchor's round-cap rule.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` state a plan that cannot be reconciled with `anchor.statement`? The anchor requires that once a sanity bead's FAIL count reaches the repository's `max_sanity_rounds` (5 when unset) the hook escalates to the phase lead rather than reopening the checked bead. A plan conflicts if it says FAILs are reopened without limit, never escalates, hard-codes the cap with no repository setting, uses a different default, or waits until the count exceeds the cap. A plan that describes reopening on a FAIL but says nothing about a round limit is silent about the cap, not in conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item is about a different subject and says nothing about sanity FAIL handling or round limits.
criteria.unclear: It is not possible to tell what subject the item is about.
criteria.yes: The item is about sanity FAIL handling or the number of allowed sanity FAIL rounds.

relevant.instructions: Is `item.text` about the same subject as `anchor.statement`, namely what the sanity close hook does after a sanity FAIL and how many FAIL rounds are allowed before the lead is involved? A different approach to the same subject still counts as the same subject. Judge subject only.
